name: Weber Auto & Truck Parts,Inc.
old_description: Use our inventory search. If you do not find what you are looking for, please contact us and we will help you find what you are looking for.
about:
Weber Auto & Truck Parts, Inc. has operated as a family-owned auto salvage and parts business in Derry, New Hampshire since 1966. Now in its second generation, the company sits on more than 10 acres near the intersection of Interstate 93 and Route 28, serving customers six days a week.

The yard stocks foreign and domestic used auto parts managed through a computerized inventory system, and also buys scrap metal and non‑ferrous materials. In addition to parts sales, Weber Auto offers junk‑vehicle removal any day of the week, sells used batteries with a core‑exchange program, and carries used tires and rims priced by tread depth.

Customers range from individual vehicle owners and independent repair shops to scrap processors. The business is open to the general public and advertises top‑dollar payment for junk cars and scrap metal, positioning it as both a retail parts outlet and a recycling collector for the southern New Hampshire region.

The company emphasizes its computerized inventory and the convenience of daily junk‑car pickup as key differentiators, backed by a limited 30‑day warranty on most parts sold.

name: Weld Fab Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: WeldFab has the equipment and expertise to produce metal fabrications for your business needs, at the level of quality you demand.
about:
Weld Fab Manufacturing Corporation operates from Slinger, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1990 as a small weldment shop. The family-owned business began with minor welding projects and expanded steadily over the following decade.

Today the company runs a 50,000-square-foot facility equipped for sheet metal fabrication, laser cutting, turret punching, robotic and manual welding, CNC machining, tube bending, and precision forming. Its equipment roster includes multiple Amada brake presses, fiber lasers, turret punches, Miller robotic welding cells, Fadal vertical machining centers, and Miyano live-tooling lathes. The shop works with carbon steel, aluminum, stainless steel, galvanized and galvannealed sheet from 0.020 to 1.00 inch thick, and handles parts from hand-sized components to room-sized weldments.

Weld Fab serves a broad range of industrial customers, though the company does not list specific sectors on its public pages. Its capabilities are geared toward original equipment manufacturers and fabricators requiring custom metal parts, welded assemblies, and machined components.

The firm emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system, which integrates SolidWorks and Dr ABE simulation for bending validation, and uses a Romer arm with Virtek laser scanning for real-time inspection. Management says this end-to-end QC process reduces handling time, identifies material alternatives, and secures custom tooling before production starts.

name: Weld House
old_description: Bold pieces for bold spaces. Our furniture is designed to make a statement and built to last.
about:
Weld House was founded in 2011 by Joel Hester in Phoenix, Arizona. The business began as a garage hobby in 2005 while Hester worked in graphic design and commercial printing, a career that spanned more than 20 years and instilled a discipline for tight tolerances and detail-oriented production.

Today the company operates a nearly 30,000-square-foot, climate-controlled manufacturing facility staffed by nearly two dozen employees. It focuses exclusively on commercial custom welding, welded furniture fabrication, and contract furniture manufacturing, producing pieces that ship across the United States nearly every day and have reached customers in Europe, Japan, Australia, and the Middle East.

Weld House serves the commercial furniture trade, supplying designers, specifiers, and end-users in hospitality, workplace, and public-space projects. Its client base spans national accounts and international buyers who require scalable production and reliable logistics.

Hester credits the company's evolution to clients who pushed the team into new design territory, a dynamic that still drives its most recognizable pieces. The printing heritage translates into a process-oriented approach that emphasizes on-time delivery within narrow windows and consistent quality at scale.

name: Wellbeloved woodworks
old_description: Wellbeloved Woodworks sells handmade furniture, guitars and caskets made by Dylan Weller of Santa Fe, New Mexico.  Using traditional woodworking techniques, each piece is hand made and hand crafted (including table, night stand, chair, bookcase, bench, dresser, armoire, bed, side table).
about:
Wellbeloved Woodworks operates from Santa Fe, New Mexico, where woodworker Dylan Weller handcrafts furniture, guitars, and caskets using traditional techniques. The business began as a one-person shop focused on hand-tool joinery and custom woodworking.

The workshop produces a range of solid-wood pieces including tables, nightstands, chairs, bookcases, benches, dressers, armoires, beds, and side tables, as well as guitar bodies and caskets. Work is executed with hand tools and traditional joinery methods such as dovetail and mitered construction, bookmatching, and live-edge milling. Custom cabinetry, such as cherry kitchen cabinets, is also offered.

Clients have included the New Mexico House of Representatives, for which the shop built a walnut speaker’s gavel, along with residential customers seeking custom furniture and musicians commissioning guitar bodies. The product list also shows Shaker-inspired cradles, credenzas, and dining tables, indicating a base of individual and institutional buyers.

Weller emphasizes that each piece is hand made and hand crafted using traditional woodworking techniques, a distinction he attributes to the use of hand tools and time-honored joinery rather than automated production.

about:
Welton Technology LLC was founded in 2018 in Leominster, Massachusetts. The privately held company employs approximately 280 engineers, researchers, and product designers who focus on removing friction from the software stack.

The company provides an enterprise-grade technology platform that combines AI and machine learning, cloud infrastructure, API gateway and mesh, data and analytics, security and compliance, and CI/CD and DevOps tooling. The platform runs on a global network of more than 320 points of presence, delivers a 99.9% uptime SLA with sub-10-millisecond average latency, and has powered over 40,000 products across 90 countries since launch. Capabilities include fine-tunable foundation models, vector databases, RAG pipelines, real-time inference APIs, autoscaling compute, managed Kubernetes, global CDN, Terraform-native infrastructure as code, rate limiting, JWT authentication, GraphQL federation, Kafka-compatible streaming, lakehouse architecture, automated vulnerability scanning, SAST/DAST integration, secret management, GitOps workflows, blue-green deployments, and feature flags with rollback in seconds.

Welton serves engineering teams in regulated and high-growth sectors, including fintech, healthcare SaaS, e-commerce, and developer tools. Reference customers cited on the site include a Series C fintech in San Francisco, a healthcare SaaS platform in London, an e-commerce enterprise in Amsterdam, and a developer-tools startup in Berlin.

The company positions its platform as invisible infrastructure that lets teams deploy AI into production in hours rather than months, unify multi-cloud environments under a single control plane, and achieve zero-trust security without sacrificing deployment speed. Its stated aim is to deliver reliability at any scale for developers, data teams, and enterprise operators who refuse to compromise on speed, security, or scalability.

name: Wengerd Wood Inc
old_description: Making accurate components for your project can be difficult, time-consuming, and labor intensive. Located in Northeast Ohio, Wengerd Wood Inc’s CNC routing service makes your job easy by providing accurate and repeatable parts in a time frame that works for you.
about:
Wengerd Wood Inc operates from Dundee, Ohio, providing CNC routing services to customers across the region. The company focuses on precision cutting and engraving for a variety of materials.

The shop runs multiple CNC routers and laser systems, handling solid wood, plywood, and plastics. Its capabilities include CNC routing, CNC engraving, laser engraving, and engineering/drafting support. The facility uses CAD software for programming and design, enabling repeatable accuracy and quick proof approvals. With several machines, the company can scale from single prototypes to runs of hundreds of cabinets, allocating machine time to meet varying timelines.

Wengerd Wood serves cabinet manufacturers, woodworking shops, and custom fabricators who need accurate components. The company’s software is tailored for high-volume cabinet part engineering, and it also offers material sourcing, painting, staining, and finishing through partner connections, positioning itself as a single source from raw material to ready-for-assembly parts.

The company emphasizes its investment in equipment and software as key differentiators, stating that multiple machines provide flexibility for almost any job size and that its CAD workflow delivers clear proofs and repeatable precision. It also highlights a one-stop-shop model that coordinates finishing services to simplify the supply chain for customers.

about:
Wesdon Automotive, a division of Wesdon Industries LLC, has operated from West Bend, Wisconsin since 2004. The company was established to supply premium exhaust components for a wide range of vehicles, though the founders are not publicly named. Ownership details beyond the LLC structure are not disclosed.

The West Bend facility produces exhaust kits, flex pipes, stamped X- and Y-pipes, and a variety of bolt-on tips. Processes include stainless-steel fabrication, chrome and black-chrome plating, powder coating, and high-temperature black coating. The company emphasizes in-house manufacturing but does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Wesdon serves the automotive, truck, off-road, SUV, UTV, marine, RV, motorcycle, and powersport markets. Its products are sold directly to consumers through Amazon, eBay, and Walmart storefronts, and the brand sponsors race cars as a demonstration of performance credibility.

The company states its goal is to exceed customer expectations through a commitment to service, quality, and delivery at an affordable price. Free shipping to the continental United States is offered on all orders, and the product line includes multiple finish options such as polished, black chrome, graphite black, and matte black.

name: West Michigan Plastics
old_description: We strive to meet customer’s expectations for quality molded, engineered plastic products.
about:
West Michigan Plastics, Inc. was founded in 1986 and incorporated in 1991 in Holland, Michigan. The company began as a custom injection molder of engineered thermoplastic resins and has grown to operate a 16,250‑square‑foot facility in the same community.

The shop specializes in high‑precision injection molding for engineered thermoplastics, supported by automated work cells that run 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its equipment roster includes small, medium, and large presses, along with automated vision inspection systems and in‑cell data collection for statistical process control. The team also provides design optimization, material selection, tool construction, mold‑flow analysis, and applications engineering.

Customers span automotive, government, medical, construction, furniture, agriculture, and electronics sectors. The company has held government contracts since the early 1990s and entered the medical market in 2002, building a diversified base that relies on its ability to deliver complex, high‑performance plastic components.

Its stated differentiators include rapid turnaround from round‑the‑clock automation, a focus on highly engineered custom parts, and proactive collaboration on design, materials, and tooling to prevent defects.

name: West Virginia Electric Corporation
old_description: WV Electric has been in service since 1946, providing years of engineering, automation and electrical system services. We have in-house engineering and construction teams for turn-key solutions.
about:
West Virginia Electric Corporation has operated from Fairmont, West Virginia since 1946. The company is owned by Victory of West Virginia, a group that includes six other subsidiary businesses. Founded as an electrical service provider, it has grown into a multi-discipline engineering and construction firm.

The firm delivers turnkey design-build solutions through registered professional engineers in electrical, mechanical, civil, and structural disciplines. Its in-house capabilities include a UL-listed panel shop that designs and manufactures custom control panels, an AISC-certified structural fabrication shop with a paint facility, and teams for PLC and HMI programming, fiber-optic installation, arc-flash analysis, and legacy-system modernization. The company also provides on-site technical support, systems integration, and material-handling system design using CAD software.

WV Electric serves the energy and utilities sector, as well as automation and material-handling industries. Its customer base spans industrial facilities across the United States that require custom electrical systems, automation upgrades, and ongoing maintenance.

The company distinguishes itself by designing and building custom solutions rather than relying on off-the-shelf products. Its combination of engineering, fabrication, and installation under one roof allows it to support outdated legacy systems and deliver integrated projects with a single point of responsibility.
